Hi Neha — great call, thanks. Answers below: 

1) Latency: aim for p95 end-to-end generation <= 250ms for typical short prompts (~120 tokens). Token-by-token streaming should start within 100ms of request and sustain <50ms token latency if possible.
2) Throughput: sustained baseline 150 qps, expected steady-state 300 qps during business hours, peak bursts up to 600 qps for promo spikes. Concurrency: expect ~60 concurrent active generation sessions at peak.
3) Cost preference: would like to evaluate A10G vs H100 tradeoffs. We prefer lower unit cost but can't compromise p95 during bursts.
4) Security: Dedicated is fine; must be VPC+KMS, SOC2 compliant. Procurement loop: CC'd procurement for contract/PO questions.

If you send sizing options we can review; ideally we'll do a 2-hour validation run during our staging window next week.

Thanks,
Samir

Subject: Dedicated sizing options (A10G vs H100) + validation plan

Samir / Neha — attaching two quick artifacts: 1) a CSV with synthetic bench results (shopwell_benchmarks_qps_vs_latency.csv) and 2) a short PDF that outlines two sizing options. High-level summary below.

Assumptions: prompt ~120 tokens, model = open-qa-13b (quantized FP16/INT8 as applicable), streaming enabled, KV cache warm for repeated prefixes. Network egress minimal (no heavy context loads).

Option A — Cost-conscious (A10G-based):
- Recommended cluster: 4 x A10G (reserved into Dedicated pool)
- Expected reserved throughput: ~220 qps sustained (with smart batching) per cluster; with autoscale burst to 600 qps across pool if allowing short burst nodes.
- Latency expectations: p95 generation ~180-260ms (token 1 latency ~90-120ms), token latency ~40-60ms once streaming starts.
- Concurrency per GPU: ~12-20 concurrent sessions depending on prompt variance and batching efficiency.
- Cost: lower hourly and predictable with reserved capacity.

Option B — Performance-first (H100-based):
- Recommended cluster: 2 x H100 (larger memory & compute)
- Expected reserved throughput: ~400 qps sustained per cluster, with headroom for 800+ qps bursts across pool.
- Latency expectations: p95 generation <140-200ms (token 1 latency ~50-80ms), token latency ~20-35ms for streaming.
- Concurrency per GPU: ~40+ concurrent sessions when using larger batch strategies + KV cache.
- Cost: higher unit cost but better p95 headroom for bursty workloads.

Sizing notes / operational levers:
- Autoscaling: recommend conservative reserved baseline + burst nodes to handle promos.
- Batching & latency tradeoff: we can tune max_batch_time to favor latency during peak (less batching) or cost during steady-state (more batching).
- KV caching: prefix caching can reduce compute for repeated prompts; reduces p95 especially for multi-turn sessions.
- Streaming: our runtime provides token-level flush control; we typically incur small additional CPU network overhead for streaming, but GPU latency dominates.

Validation plan (2-hour run):
- Goal: validate p95 <= 250ms under 600 qps bursts and sustained 300 qps, with streaming enabled.
- Steps: provision chosen Dedicated pool, run synthetic workload (mirrors ShopWell's prompt distribution), capture per-token latency, p95/p99, throughput, GPU utilization.
- Artifacts: bench CSV, perf flame graphs, and recommended config.

Attached: shopwell_benchmarks_qps_vs_latency.csv (synthetic runs), dedicated_capacity_options_v2.pdf

Next steps: Samir — please confirm which option to validate (A10G or H100) and preferred window next week. We'll schedule SE time (Dev/Aditya) and ops to spin up the pool.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
